reference: Bash's documented type/help builtin behavior and the ipcmk interface documented in docs/sol-ipcmk.md are the oracle for contract cases. No resource-creation parity oracle was executed. A future isolated operation suite should compare GNU util-linux ipcmk where syntax overlaps and independently inspect and remove only objects created by the fixture using Linux IPC metadata APIs.
coverage: Contract: ipcmk is registered as a Bash builtin and is visible through type -t.
Contract: Bash help exposes the documented resource forms and POSIX mode/persistence notes.
Deferred: System V shared memory creation, metadata, and owned-object cleanup.
Deferred: System V semaphore array creation, metadata, and owned-object cleanup.
Deferred: System V message queue creation, metadata, and owned-object cleanup.
Deferred: named POSIX shared memory creation, size/mode, collision behavior, and unlink.
Deferred: named POSIX semaphore creation, initial value/mode, collision behavior, and unlink.
Deferred: named POSIX message queue creation, default attributes/mode, collision behavior, and unlink.
exclusions: No ipcmk creation or parsing operation was invoked; this task forbids dangerous loadable operations on the host, and IPC operations require a separately approved disposable VM or reviewed mock.

No raw output from GNU ipcmk is compared because System V identifiers are allocated dynamically and POSIX operations create kernel objects; operation coverage needs a purpose-built independent inspector and owned-object cleanup inside an isolated VM.
No ipcctl or other loadable was used. The suite is not marked optional because ipcmk is not listed in bash-loadables-optional.list.

cases.purpose: Use Bash type -t to confirm ipcmk is exposed as a shell builtin without invoking its implementation.
Use Bash help to check the documented command synopsis, all resource forms, POSIX umask behavior, and persistence statement without invoking ipcmk.
cases.script:
[[ $(type -t ipcmk) == builtin ]]
doc=$(help ipcmk)
[[ $doc == *"Create System V or named POSIX IPC resources."* ]]
[[ $doc == *"ipcmk [-p mode] -M size"* ]]
[[ $doc == *"ipcmk [-p mode] -S number"* ]]
[[ $doc == *"ipcmk [-p mode] -Q"* ]]
[[ $doc == *"ipcmk [-p mode] -n /name (-m size|-s|-q)"* ]]
[[ $doc == *"POSIX permissions are filtered by umask; semaphore initial value is zero."* ]]
[[ $doc == *"Successful resources persist until explicitly removed or unlinked."* ]]
printf 'documented ipcmk help markers present\n'

cases.purpose: Verify creation and kernel metadata for one IPC_PRIVATE System V shared memory segment, then remove only the ID returned by the fixture.
cases.reason: Requires a disposable Linux VM with a fresh private IPC namespace and GNU util-linux ipcmk. A future test should create a small segment (for example, 4096 bytes at mode 0600), parse its returned ID, independently verify size, mode, and owner with shmctl(IPC_STAT), then remove and confirm absence with shmctl(IPC_RMID/IPC_STAT). Do not inspect or remove any pre-existing ID.

cases.purpose: Verify a System V semaphore array's requested count and mode, then remove only the array created by the fixture.
cases.reason: Requires a disposable Linux VM with a fresh private IPC namespace and GNU util-linux ipcmk. A future test should create a small array (for example, two semaphores at mode 0600), parse its returned ID, independently check sem_nsems, mode, and owner with semctl(IPC_STAT), then remove and confirm absence with semctl(IPC_RMID/IPC_STAT). Use no existing semaphore IDs.

cases.purpose: Verify System V message queue creation, empty initial state, and requested mode, then remove only the created queue.
cases.reason: Requires a disposable Linux VM with a fresh private IPC namespace and GNU util-linux ipcmk. A future test should create one queue at a small explicit mode, parse the returned ID, independently verify owner, mode, and zero queued messages with msgctl(IPC_STAT), then remove and confirm absence with msgctl(IPC_RMID/IPC_STAT). Never target an unrelated queue.

cases.purpose: Verify named POSIX shared memory size, umask-filtered mode, exclusive creation, and cleanup of the fixture-owned name.
cases.reason: Requires a disposable Linux VM with isolated POSIX IPC backing storage, a unique slash-prefixed name, and GNU util-linux ipcmk. A future test should create a small named object under a controlled umask, inspect its owner, exact length, and mode through shm_open/fstat, confirm a second exclusive create fails without changing the object, and shm_unlink only the name it created.

cases.purpose: Verify named POSIX semaphore initial value, umask-filtered mode, exclusive creation, and cleanup of the fixture-owned name.
cases.reason: Requires a disposable Linux VM with isolated POSIX IPC backing storage, a unique slash-prefixed name, and GNU util-linux ipcmk. A future test should create under a controlled umask, independently confirm sem_getvalue is zero and inspect owner/mode, verify a second exclusive create fails without taking ownership, and sem_unlink only the name created by the fixture.

cases.purpose: Verify named POSIX message queue default attributes, umask-filtered mode, exclusive creation, and cleanup of the fixture-owned name.
cases.reason: Requires a disposable Linux VM with isolated POSIX IPC backing storage, a unique slash-prefixed name, and GNU util-linux ipcmk. A future test should independently inspect mq_getattr for zero queued messages and positive kernel-default capacities, inspect owner/mode under a controlled umask, confirm a second exclusive create fails, and mq_unlink only the fixture-owned name.
